verses.108:3: Falaram contra mim com língua enganadora, e com palavras de ódio me cercaram: * e me combateram sem motivo.

verses.108:6: Estabelecei sobre ele um pecador: * e {diabolus} {stet} à sua direita.
verses.108:7: Quando for julgado, saia condenado: * e a sua oração se torne pecado.
verses.108:8: {fiant8} poucos os seus dias: * e outro receba {episcopatum}.
verses.108:9: {fiant9} órfãos os seus filhos: * e a sua mulher, viúva.
verses.108:10: {nutantes} os seus filhos, e mendiguem: * e sejam lançados fora das suas habitações.
verses.108:11: {scrutetur} {fenerator} {substantia}: * e estranhos saqueiem os seus trabalhos.
verses.108:12: Não haja {adjutor} para ele: * nem haja quem tenha piedade dos seus órfãos.
verses.108:13: {fiant13} {nati} {interitum}: * numa só geração se apague o seu nome.

verses.108:17: E perseguiu o homem carente, e mendigo, * e o compungido de coração, para lhe dar a morte.

verses.108:23: Como a sombra quando declina, {ablatus}: * e fui sacudido como os gafanhotos.

decisions.why: *tacére* with an object is 'to pass over in silence' (μὴ παρασιωπήσῃς). *laudem meam* is open: the praise I give God, or my good name that God should speak for (MS1932's note: 'do not cease to show my innocence'). The transitive *calar* keeps both ('calar a verdade' = keep the truth unsaid) in the Latin's three words. The glossary's reflexive *calar-se* (tacére, 27:1, 31:3, 49:20) needs a preposition here, and *sobre* adds a word the Latin lacks. DRB 'be not thou silent in thy praise'; MS1932 *não cales o meu louvor*.

options.label: não vos caleis sobre o meu louvor

forms.tacueris: não vos caleis sobre o meu louvor

options.label: não deixeis em silêncio o meu louvor

forms.tacueris: não deixeis em silêncio o meu louvor

options.note: the Greek's 'pass over in silence' made explicit; longer

decisions.why: *super* (place) → *sobre* is the glossary's row, and the image is of mouths gaping over the speaker. DRB and MS1932 read it as hostility, 'against me' (ἐπ᾿ ἐμέ can mean both). *sobre mim* holds both; *contra mim* would also merge it with *advérsum me* in 108:3 and 108:5. The Latin's singular *apértum est* with two subjects becomes the plural, which is Portuguese grammar.

options.label: contra mim
options.note: DRB 'against me', MS1932; merges with *advérsum me*

decisions.latin: mala pro bonis: * et ódium pro dilectióne mea
decisions.why: *mala pro bonis* is word for word 37:21 (*retribuem males por bens*), so the first colon copies it (rule 6). The second *pro* is kept as *por* too, so that the Latin's repetition stays and the verse reads as one exchange twice. The risk: *ódio pelo meu amor* taken alone could be heard as 'hatred of my love'; after *males por bens* the exchange should be heard. MS1932 has *em troca de* in both colons; that is the option if a reader mishears.

options.label: por … em troca do
options.note: the second colon unambiguous; the repetition lost

options.label: em troca de … em troca do

decisions.latin: et diábolus stet a dextris ejus
decisions.why: The Latin carries the Greek διάβολος over as a name, as a Latin ear hears it: 'the devil' (DRB). The Greek also means 'slanderer, accuser' (Hebrew *satan*, 'adversary'), and the Greek ties it to ἐνδιαβάλλω in 108:4, 20, 29. The Latin does not make that tie (it has *detráhere* there), and an 'accuser' would read the Hebrew into the Latin. So *o diabo*. MS1932's *o demônio* is another word (*dæmónium*, 95:5).

options.label: o diabo
options.note: draft — the Latin's word; DRB 'the devil'

options.label: o acusador
options.note: the Greek word's first sense and the Hebrew's; interprets the Latin

decisions.why: The *stare* row gives *estar de pé*, and the posture matters: the accuser stood at the right hand in court. But *esteja de pé à sua direita* makes the colon 16 syllables against the Latin's 10, and the jussive *esteja* with *à direita* already says where he stands. MS1932 *esteja o demônio à sua direita*. The row's full form is the option.

decisions.latin: Fiant dies ejus pauci … Fiant fílii ejus órphani … Fiant nati ejus in intéritum
decisions.why: Three verses open on *Fiant*, and the Portuguese opens all three on *Sejam* so that the anaphora stays (rule 2). The glossary's row for *fíeri* + adjective asks for *tornar-se* (19:4, a Latinist major against *seja*). Here the verb is a curse, and *Sejam poucos os seus dias* is heard as 'may they become few'. *Tornem-se* would be exact, but it is heavy three times running, and *Tornem-se órfãos os seus filhos* is not how Portuguese says it. MS1932 varies (*Sejam abreviados … Fiquem … Sejam exterminados*). 108:15 *Fiant contra Dóminum* is a place, so it takes *Estejam*.

options.label: Tornem-se … Fiquem … Sejam
options.note: the becoming spelled out; the anaphora lost

decisions.why: The Latin's word is *episcopátus* (Lewis & Short: 'the office and dignity of a bishop', citing this verse), and this is the line St Peter applies to Judas in Acts 1:20 (in the Vulgate: *episcopatum eius accipiat alter*). The Greek ἐπισκοπή is 'office of oversight'. *O seu episcopado* keeps the Latin's word and the apostolic reading the Church gave it; DRB keeps 'bishopric'. A Brazilian ear will find it pointed, and the Latin is pointed too. *cargo* is plain and loses the word; MS1932's *ministério* interprets.

*nutáre* is to sway, totter, waver (L&S); the Greek is σαλευόμενοι, the root that 54:23 *fluctuátio* already renders as *vacilar*. *transférre → transportar* is settled (D43). The participle stays at the head, as in the Latin. DRB 'carried about vagabonds' and MS1932 *Andem vagabundos dum lugar para outro* read the Hebrew's wandering into it, and they drop *transférre*.

options.label: Sejam levados daqui para ali, vacilantes,

forms.nutantes: Sejam levados daqui para ali, vacilantes,

options.note: plainer verb for persons; adds 'from here to there'; breaks D43

options.label: Andem errantes de um lugar para outro

forms.nutantes: Andem errantes de um lugar para outro

options.note: MS1932's sense; the Hebrew's wandering; drops *transférre*

decisions.why: *scrutári → sondar* is the row (7:10, 63:7, Ps 118). Here it is a creditor searching out every last possession. *Sonde* keeps the row. *Esquadrinhe* is more vivid for the ransacking, and the row lists it as its option; MS1932 has *dê caça a*.

Lewis & Short: 'one who lends on interest, a money-lender … with an odious secondary idea, a usurer'. *usura → usura* is the glossary's row (14:5), and *o usurário* keeps the family. MS1932 and DRB ('userer') have the same word. *o credor* is plainer and loses the odium the Latin word has.

options.label: o usurário
options.note: draft — MS1932, DRB; the usura row's family

decisions.why: D39 names this verse: *substántia* here is property, and it is decided locally (the row's *o meu ser* is for a person's being). The Greek πάντα ὅσα ὑπάρχει αὐτῷ is 'all that he has'. *todos os seus bens* is MS1932's wording; DRB's 'all his substance' is the old English sense of property, and Portuguese *substância* does not carry it.

options.label: todos os seus bens
options.note: draft — D39's note for this verse; MS1932

decisions.why: *adjútor → auxílio* is the row (open, for Gustavo; uniform in 14 places). Here the Latin is 'let there be no helper for him'. *Não haja auxílio para ele* keeps the row and the Latin's *sit … sit* repetition (*Não haja … nem haja*). The Latinist has asked for the agent noun in other psalms; *quem o auxilie* makes the person audible and matches the second colon's *quem tenha piedade*.

options.label: quem o auxilie
options.note: the helper as a person; parallels the second colon

options.label: auxiliador
options.note: the agent noun the Latinist asked for elsewhere

decisions.why: The Latin varies *fílii* (108:9, 108:10) and *nati* (108:13), as the Greek does (υἱοί / τέκνα). Portuguese has no plain pair: *os que dele nasceram* keeps the root but adds four syllables, and *prole* and *descendência* are taken or learned (D32 *semen → descendência*). So *os seus filhos*, the merge DRB avoids ('posterity') and MS1932 makes. *in intéritum* is 'into destruction' (*intéritus → destruição*, the row). A bare *Sejam para a destruição* is ambiguous in Portuguese (it can mean 'for destroying others'), so *entregues à* is supplied, as 43:22b's *somos entregues à morte* supplied it for *mortificámur*. MS1932 *Sejam exterminados* turns the noun into a verb.

options.label: os seus filhos … entregues à destruição
os que dele nasceram … para a destruição
options.note: the root of *nati* kept, no participle supplied; +3 syllables

decisions.why: *contra* here is 'facing' (ἔναντι κυρίου, 'before the Lord'), as at 50:5 *contra me*, which D44 settled as *diante de mim*. *contra o Senhor* would be heard as 'against the Lord', a wrong sense. The subject is left unnamed, as in the Latin: the sins of 108:14, or the fathers and mother. MS1932 supplies *(os seus crimes)* as a gloss.

options.label: diante do Senhor
options.note: draft — D44's *contra* = ἐνώπιον; DRB 'before the lord'

options.label: perante o Senhor
options.note: the same sense; keeps it apart from other *diante de*

decisions.latin: et intrávit sicut aqua in interióra ejus
decisions.why: The Latin leaves the subject of *intrávit* unexpressed. It is the curse he put on, and MS1932 names it (*e ela penetrou*). Portuguese can leave it unexpressed too, and the sense still comes through from *vestiu a maldição*. Kept unexpressed, so as not to add a word the Latin lacks. If a reader hears 'he entered', *ela entrou* is the fix.

options.label: entrou
options.note: draft — subject unexpressed, as the Latin

options.label: ela entrou
options.note: the curse named as subject, as MS1932

decisions.why: The Greek is εἰς τὰ ἔγκατα αὐτοῦ, the same word the Greek has at 50:12 *in viscéribus meis*, which D44 settled as *entranhas*. By D15's test (one Greek word, one Portuguese word) *interióra* joins it. MS1932 and DRB also have entrails. The literal *no seu interior* is abstract where the Latin is bodily, beside *ossos*.

options.label: entranhas
options.note: draft — D44 víscera's word (same Greek); MS1932, DRB

decisions.latin: sicut óleum in óssibus ejus … propter óleum
decisions.why: *óleum → óleo* is what the psalter already has (44:8 *óleo de alegria*, 88:21 *o meu óleo santo*). MS1932 has *azeite*, which is concrete and Brazilian, but it would split the word from the anointing verses. The same word serves both places in this psalm.

decisions.latin: et caro mea immutáta est propter óleum
decisions.why: The Latin says 'on account of oil' (δι᾿ ἔλαιον). Whether that means 'for lack of oil' (MS1932's reading, and the Hebrew's 'without fat') or something else, the Latin does not say, and the translation must not settle it. *por causa do óleo* keeps it open. *immutáre → mudar*, as 72:21 *foram mudados*.

options.label: por falta de óleo
options.note: MS1932's gloss made text; resolves the Latin

decisions.why: *opus* is 'work' (ἔργον). The Hebrew has 'wages' here, and MS1932's *o lucro* follows that sense. The Latin says *opus*, so *a obra*: 'this is what they do', or read with the curses before it, 'this is what they have earned'. The Latin leaves both open.

options.label: o salário
options.note: the Hebrew's sense; not the Latin

decisions.why: *fac mecum* has no object in the Latin (the Greek adds ἔλεος, 'mercy'). The row *fácere cum → tratar* (118:124) works when a manner follows (*segundo a vossa misericórdia*); here only *propter nomen tuum* follows. *Agi comigo* falls to rule 3 (*agi* = 'I acted'). *fazei comigo* is the Latin as it stands, open-ended as the Latin is. DRB 'do with me'; MS1932 paraphrases (*toma à tua conta a minha defesa*).

options.label: fazei comigo
options.note: draft — the Latin's open verb; DRB

options.label: tratai-me
options.note: the *fácere cum* row; wants a manner after it

decisions.why: *auferre → tirar* is settled (D41). The Greek ἀντανῃρέθην is 'I was taken away'. *fui tirado* keeps the row. It is a little thin without a 'from where', and the Latin has none either. *fui levado* is plainer but is *addúcere*'s verb (D42).

decisions.latin: Et sciant quia manus tua hæc: * et tu, Dómine, fecísti eam
decisions.why: The second colon has no *quia* of its own. It can be a second thing they are to know ('and that you did it', as DRB and MS1932 supply) or the psalmist's own statement ('and you, Lord, have done it'). Kept without *que*, which holds both. *eam* is feminine, as *mão* is, so *a fizestes* keeps the Latin's reference: the hand, or what the hand did.

options.label: e que vós, Senhor, a fizestes

forms.eam: e que vós, Senhor, a fizestes

decisions.why: The *maledícere* row (D44: *amaldiçoar*) proposes *maldizer* wherever *benedícere* stands beside it, as 61:5 did (*bendiziam … maldiziam*), and names this verse. One root (*-dizer*) keeps the Latin's pair audible. Both verbs have no object, as in the Latin (MS1932 supplies *me*). *illi* is expressed in the Latin, so *Eles* stays. The *vós* future *bendireis* is safe under rule 3.

options.label: Eles maldirão, e vós bendireis
options.note: draft — the row's proposal for this verse (61:5)

options.label: Eles amaldiçoarão, e vós bendireis
options.note: D44's settled verb; the pair's root lost

options.label: Eles amaldiçoarão, e vós abençoareis
options.note: the everyday pair; leaves the benedícere row

decisions.why: Lewis & Short: 'a double robe to be wrapped around the body, a cloak, mantle', citing this verse (διπλοΐς). *manto* is already *opertórium*'s word (101:27, another Greek word). *capa dupla* (MS1932) keeps both the garment and the 'double', and stays apart from *manto*.

decisions.latin: Confitébor Dómino nimis in ore meo
decisions.why: *confitéri → dar graças* (D5). This is one of the three verses D5 names where it stands beside *laudáre*, and the pair is kept apart (*darei graças … o louvarei*). *nimis* has no single rendering (its row). *sem medida* is the row's rendering where it is 'beyond measure' (118:138, 45:2, 78:8; L&S). *Com a minha boca* is moved to the head so that the mediant falls on *medida* and not on *boca … medida* crowding. *Darei muitas graças* is plainer, but it makes a *muitas … muitos* echo the Latin does not have.

choices.108:3: *gratis → sem motivo* (row; 34:7, 68:5). *expugnáre → combater* (34:1). *sermo → palavra* (D15). The Latin's plural *locúti sunt* after a singular *lingua dolósa* kept.
choices.108:4: *Pro eo ut me dilígerent* → *Em vez de me amarem*: the Latin makes them the subject (the Greek infinitive and the Hebrew are 'in return for my love'; the Latin is followed). *detráhere → difamar* (D39), also 108:20 and 108:29. *ego autem → eu, porém,* (row).
choices.108:6: *constitúere → estabelecer* (row); *Estabelecei* is safe under rule 3. *a dextris ejus* here and *a dextris páuperis* in 108:31 both say *à … direita*: the psalm's turn (the devil at the wicked man's right, the Lord at the poor man's) is kept.
choices.108:7: *Cum judicátur* → *Quando for julgado* (the Portuguese future subjunctive for a general 'when'). *fiat in peccátum* → *se torne pecado* (*fíeri* in the sense of becoming: row 544).
choices.108:9: *Sejam órfãos os seus filhos: * e a sua mulher, viúva* — the Latin's gapped verb kept, marked by a comma. *órphanus / pupíllus → órfão* (row), also 108:12.
choices.108:10: *eícere → lançar fora* (row, 79:9). *habitátio → habitação* (row; *morada* is habitáculum's, D44).
choices.108:11: *aliéni → estranhos* (row), no article, as the Latin. *labóres ejus → os seus trabalhos*: the fruit of his toil, as 77:46 (a local departure from the row's *fadiga*, which there was heard as tiredness).
choices.108:13: *delére → apagar* (row); 108:13 and 108:14 have the same form *deleátur* and say *se apague* both times.
choices.108:14: *in conspéctu Dómini → à vista do Senhor* (the row's proposal, 5:9; no verb of motion here). *In memóriam rédeat → Volte à memória*: *memória* also in 108:15, where the Latin repeats it.
choices.108:15: *dispéreat → pereça de todo* (the disperíre row), with *da terra* moved before the verb so that *de todo da terra* does not pile up. *eórum → deles*, apart from the singular *ejus → seu* of the curses. *fácere misericórdiam → fazer misericórdia* (102:6 *faz misericórdias*). The Latin's 108:15 includes the Greek and Hebrew v. 16; DO has no 108:16.
choices.108:17: *inops → carente* (D38), *mendícus → mendigo* (D41), *compúnctus corde → compungido de coração* (the passive participle of the compúngi row, 29:13, 34:16). *mortificáre → dar a morte* (row); *lhe* is supplied, as 36:32.
choices.108:18: *elongáre → ficar longe* (row). The future tenses of *véniet … elongábitur* kept after the perfects: the Latin's own turn from what he did to what will come. *ela* supplied for the curse and the blessing in turn, so that each second half is not heard as 'he will come'.
choices.108:18b: *índuit maledictiónem* → *vestiu a maldição* (transitive, as the Latin: he put it on). *vestiméntum → veste* (D43), also 108:19.
choices.108:19: *Fiat ei → Seja para ele* (the *Fiat* row). *zona → cinto*: Brazilian *cinta* is also a girdle worn under clothes. *præcíngere → cingir* (17:33, 64:7).
choices.108:20: *apud Dóminum → junto do Senhor* (the apud row, 36:23; the Greek παρὰ κυρίου 'from the Lord' is not followed). *loqui mala advérsus → falar males contra* (as *mala mihi*, row 1007).
choices.108:21: *Dómine, Dómine* → *Senhor, Senhor*: the doubled cry is the Latin's and the Greek's, so it is kept. The 8:2a row refused a doubling there only because the Latin had *Dómine, Dóminus noster*. *suávis → suave* (row).
choices.108:22: *egénus → necessitado*, *pauper → pobre* (D38). *conturbáre → perturbar* (row). *intra me → dentro de mim* (38:4).
choices.108:23: *declináre* (of the shadow) → *declinar*, as 101:12 *Os meus dias declinaram como a sombra*. *locústa → gafanhoto* (77:46, 104:34).
choices.108:24: *infirmári → enfraquecer* (the infírmus / languére rows). *a jejúnio → pelo jejum*: the Latin's *a* and *propter* differ, and so do *pelo* and *por causa*.
choices.108:25: *oppróbrium → afronta* (row); *factus sum oppróbrium illis → me tornei uma afronta para eles* (30:12, 78:4). *movérunt cápita sua → moveram as suas cabeças*: the plural of the Latin, where 21:8 has the singular *caput*.
choices.108:26: The formula *Senhor, meu Deus* (row). *adjuváre → auxiliar* (row), *salvum me fac → salvai-me* (row).
choices.108:28: *insúrgere in → levantar-se contra* (row). *confúndi → ser envergonhado* (D15); *sejam envergonhados* comes first, where Portuguese puts a jussive. The Latin's second colon is 17 syllables, and the Portuguese is longer because D15's verb is. Accepted.
choices.108:29: *pudor → desonra*, *confúsio → vergonha*: the pair as 70:13 *sejam cobertos de vergonha e de desonra* (ἐντροπή / αἰσχύνη, the reveréri row). *Induántur … pudóre* → *Vistam-se de desonra*, as 34:26b.
choices.108:31: *astáre a dextris → pôr-se à direita* (the astáre row's split, 44:10b). *a persequéntibus → dos que a perseguem*: *a* is supplied (the Latin's participle has no object). DRB 'from persecutors'.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the parallels file (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932; no DM1962 section for this psalm). Glossary rows read for every controlled word. The curses of 108:6–19 are rendered as the Latin has them, jussive for jussive, with nothing softened or explained. Hard readings: 108:2 *laudem meam ne tacúeris*; 108:8 *episcopátum*; 108:10 *nutántes transferántur*; 108:13 *fiant … in intéritum*; 108:15 *contra Dóminum* = 'before'; 108:24 *propter óleum*; 108:27 the second colon without *quia*.

render.py + checks.py: hard checks pass (ids, one `*` per verse; no 108:16, as DO). Soft flags accepted: 108:28 second colon +7 (D15's *sejam envergonhados* is longer than *confundántur*; the Latin's colon is already the psalm's longest); 108:2 +6 and 108:17 +6 (Portuguese needs *se abriram* and *lhe dar a morte*); 108:15 -5 (*pro eo quod* → *porque*). Rhyme 108:7 *julgado / condenado* is the Latin's own *judicátur / condemnátus*; 108:7/108:8 *pecado / episcopado* is incidental and far apart in the verse. Readers to be run by the coordinator: claude-opus-5-5 in fresh context (latinist, stylist, ambiguity).
